content.text: InstagramLog InSign UpCloseNever miss a post from astrokirstenSign up for Instagram to stay in the loop.Sign upLog inAudio is mutedastrokirsten•FollowOriginal audioMore optionsastrokirsten 6dThey’re coming home.The Artemis II crew returns to Earth tomorrow — here’s everything you need to know.When is splashdown?🌊 Expected: Friday, April 10 at 5:07 pm PDT🇦🇺 That’s 10:07 am AEST on Saturday for Australia’s east coast.(Quick tip: Google “5:07 pm PDT to your timezone” for your local time.)Where can you watch it?Live coverage will be available on NASA platforms like NASA+, plus services like Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV, Netflix, HBO Max, and NASA’s YouTube channel.What happens before splashdown?🚀 ~24 hours before: Final correction burn adjusts their path home.🛰 42 minutes before: Crew module separates from the service module.🔥 13 minutes before: They hit Earth’s atmosphere — expect up to 6 minutes of radio silence as plasma forms around the capsule.🪂 ~3 minutes before: Parachutes deploy.🌊 Splashdown: After 10 days in space, they return home.This mission pushed humans farther than ever before — a huge step toward returning people to the Moon.Godspeed, Integrity. The final stretch is here.#ArtemisII #NASA #Splashdown #Orion #MoonLoad more commentsleftie.slayer 4dWatched your segment on Weekend Today. It was torture. You got so much wrong. You claimed the reason the escape velocity of the moon is so low is because of it's size. Totally wrong. The escape velocity formula is sqrt (2GM)/R. It is the lunar mass that dictates the escape velocity. The lunar mass is 1/81 that of Earth. The moon is also less dense. It it more silicates whereas Earth has an iron core. The other major factor is that the moon has essentially no atmosphere so no air resistance so less energy to launch. Then you went on about an SD card being ejected. Well first of all the Nikon D5 and Z9 don't use SD cards. They use compact flash cards (the D5 has a model that uses QXD also). That wasn't the cringe bit though. You claimed that the card flew so fast away because it had no resistance.
